newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down on importers' activity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down on importers' activity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly lower against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday, with importers buying greenbacks as the U.S. currency drifted higher in other Asian overseas markets, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.494 against Tuesday's T$27.489 close. Turnover was a slow US$116.5 million.
Dealers noted some inflows of foreign funds for Taiwan's stock market, which helped to offset the Taiwan dollar's depreciation.
They said the Taiwan dollar was in a downtrend in the long run despite its recent narrow-range consolidation.

"In the long term, the Taiwan dollar will tend to fall due to a firming U.S. dollar abroad, low Taiwan dollar interest rates and the apparent lack of recovery in the domestic economy," said one dealer.
"But in the near term, inflows of foreign equity funds are so strong that it is hard for the Taiwan dollar to break support at T$27.50," she said.
For the rest of the week, a narrow T$27.48-27.50 range was seen. -- James Peng (5080815)
